public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most Anthropic and OpenAI subscribers will not switch to paying for token-based API access.

statement.excerpt: Even if these companies were profitable on inference (I do not believe they are), they are dramatically, horrendously unprofitable on subscriptions, and there isn’t a chance in Hell that the majority of those subscriptions convert into token-based API users.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: there isn’t a chance in Hell
our_interpretation: Majority means more than 50% of the relevant subscription cohort.
Use subscriptions active at the post date as the baseline cohort, tracking each company separately and the combined population where possible.
Conversion means switching to paid, token-metered API use. Receiving bundled API credits or making an incidental API request does not by itself establish conversion.
No deadline is supplied. A forced migration is a possible test, not an antecedent expressly required by the speaker.
The categorical wording is assessed as a prediction of non-conversion, not as a statistically measurable zero probability.
criteria.support_condition: A definitive, completed disposition of the relevant subscription cohort shows that no more than half converted to paid token-based API use, with no remaining conversion path for the claim being assessed.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Verified cohort records show that more than half of the relevant subscriptions converted to paid token-based API use.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verified records showing that more than 50% of the fixed baseline cohort switched to paid token-metered API use would contradict the forecast. A terminal event closing further conversion, with final records showing no more than 50% converted, would support it.
